metadata.title: When Wages Rose, Why Did the Basics Cost More?
metadata.description:
A London labourer's daily wage more than doubled between the early 1500s and early 1600s. Yet a reconstructed basket of basic needs took more days' pay to cover. This illustrated history follows the changing cost of bread, fuel, soap, light and other essentials from before the Black Death to the late 19th century—and explains why a rising wage could still lose ground to prices. The figures are historical estimates expressed as wage-day equivalents, not records of a family's actual work year or a comparison with modern living costs.
